title: Safe-outputs request file
description: The machine-readable definition of docs/PIPELINE-CONTRACT.md §8 — the write-REQUESTS a session emits in place of holding a tracker credential. A separate job that does hold the credential validates them against the dispatcher-supplied pinned ticket ID and executes only the survivors.
$comment: EVERY FIELD HERE IS REPORTING, NEVER A FACT. Conforming to this schema earns a batch nothing: §8's validation rules run before any request executes, and they are the part that matters — every ticket_id (and a ticket-create's source_ticket_id) must equal the DISPATCHER-SUPPLIED pinned ID; at most one ticket-state and at most 3 ticket-create per run; raw/ready/done are never valid targets even when a caller passes them in allowed_to_states; agent:*, blocked:capacity, provenance:* and hooks-change are refused in add AND remove (and in a ticket-create's labels); a filed finding lands in the backlog carrying provenance:agent, applied BY THE EXECUTOR, never requested by the session; add+remove ≤ 10 per request; exactly one telemetry block across all comments when required. None of those is expressible in a schema, and one invalid request rejects the ENTIRE batch.

schema.description: An unrecognized schema rejects the batch. A reader that does not recognize it refuses; it does not guess.

requests.description: At most 20 per batch — a runaway or hostile session must not spray the tracker (§8 caps).

ticketId.description: The agent NAMES a ticket and the validator COMPARES it against the pinned ID; the value is never used to address anything. A mismatch is an attempted retarget, not a typo.

body.description: Non-empty markdown, ≤ 16 000 chars. The telemetry block (§4) travels as one of these.

ticketState.description: At most one of these per run — a run advances the ticket once. Several transitions in one batch is either confusion or an attempt to land somewhere by way of somewhere else.

to.description: A canonical state key from linear.stateIds — never a UUID, never a display name. `raw`, `ready`, `done` and `needsApproval` are excluded here AND refused by the validator however the caller is configured: ready would be self-approval (§5), done would be a session claiming its own merge (§5, §6), and needsApproval is the AI review's own conclusion — a session reporting it would be issuing a verdict on its own work. The enum is the belt; the validator's refusal is the braces the caller cannot unbuckle.

ticketLabel.description: add + remove combined are capped at 10 by the validator (§8 caps) — a cross-list total a schema cannot express.

ticketCreate.description: The FLAT finding shape of `ticket-create`: ask a credential-holding executor to FILE a single follow-up finding ticket. Discriminated from `planCreate` (the tree shape) by carrying `title`+`body` rather than `epic`+`children` — both are `type: ticket-create`, and exactly one branch matches. The session never creates the ticket itself: it names its OWN pinned ticket as `source_ticket_id` (compared to the pin, never used to address anything), and the executor creates a NEW ticket in the backlog (linear.findingTicket.landing), applies `provenance:agent`, notifies the owner, and refuses every dispatcher/human-owned label — none of which the session can set. At most 3 per run, and unavailable unless linear.findingTicket is configured (§8 caps).

title.description: One line: the finding stated as a title. The executor is the only party that sets the new ticket's identity, state, provenance and assignee.

body.description: Non-empty markdown — what was found, where, and why it was out of scope. The executor prepends a provenance line naming the filing session's source ticket, so the new ticket always carries where it came from.

labels.description: Optional ordinary labels to propose (track:*, effort:*). Dispatcher/human-owned classes (agent:*, blocked:*, provenance:*, hooks-change) are excluded by labelList and refused by the executor. `provenance:agent` is applied BY THE EXECUTOR, never requested here — a session that could request its own provenance is the shape §5 exists to prevent.

planCreate.description: The TREE shape of `ticket-create`: a planning session PROPOSES an epic and its children as one request; a credential-holding executor validates the tree, runs the Definition-of-Ready gate on every child, and materialises it. Discriminated from the flat finding shape by carrying `epic`+`children` rather than `title`+`body`. The session sets NO field that carries authority: the executor files the epic in the backlog (linear.findingTicket.landing) with executor-applied `provenance:agent`, files each child in the same backlog with `provenance:epic` and `parentId` FORCED to the epic it just created in this batch, and turns `depends_on` ordinals into blockedBy relations. Nothing becomes dispatchable until a person moves the epic out of intake (§4/§5). One malformed or DoR-failing child rejects the WHOLE tree — nothing is created (§8 all-or-nothing). Available only when linear.findingTicket is configured; at most one plan per run.

children.description: The child tickets, in dependency order. The hard schema ceiling is 20; the executor enforces its own tighter per-run cap (MAX_PLAN_CHILDREN, mirroring the flat kind's cap-of-3 as a code constant rather than a delivery.json budget). A plan legitimately IS a tree, so the cap is one epic and a bounded number of children — a flood guard, not a limit to raise.

planEpic.description: The epic the tree hangs from. The executor creates it in the backlog with `provenance:agent` — an epic a session drafted is agent-authored, and by §5 rule 1 `provenance:agent` never auto-approves, so the epic cannot approve itself. The session supplies only the words; identity, state, provenance and assignee are the executor's.

title.description: One line — the epic stated as a title.

body.description: The PRD/epic markdown that becomes the epic's description.

planChild.description: One child ticket. `body` is the full markdown with the template's `## Acceptance criteria` etc.; the executor runs check_ticket_dor.py --strict on the built ticket and REFUSES to create any child that fails, rejecting the whole tree. The executor forces `provenance:epic` and the parent link — the session cannot supply a parent id, which would otherwise let it name an already-approved epic and have its children auto-approve.

title.description: One line — the child stated as a title. The DoR gate enforces its own tighter title limit.

body.description: Non-empty markdown carrying the template's five sections. The DoR gate judges it.

labels.description: Ordinary labels only (track:*, effort:*). Dispatcher/human-owned classes are excluded by labelList; `provenance:epic` is applied BY THE EXECUTOR, never requested here.

depends_on.description: 0-indexed ordinals into THIS request's `children` array (child at index 1 with `depends_on: [0]` is blocked by child index 0). The executor turns them into Linear blockedBy relations, refusing any ordinal out of range, self-referential, or forming a cycle.

items.description: Canonical label keys from linear.labels.ids (§6). Dispatcher- and human-owned classes are excluded here and refused by the validator in BOTH lists: a session setting agent:needs-human — or clearing agent:blocked — is a session editing its own supervision.

labelList.description: May be empty. Unknown keys are refused by the validator; only keys present in linear.labels.ids resolve to an ID.
